title: Silver, Wood and Limewood: A Slow Week in Banská Štiavnica and the Spiš Towns

bestPeriod.window: the second half of September — warm days, tajchy still swimmable in the first week, no coach parties in Levoča
bestPeriod.avoid: late July–August in Banská Štiavnica (Slovak domestic peak, the tajchy are full) and any Monday, when almost every museum in the country closes

food.note: €140–€210 (€20–€30/day — guesthouse dinners are the cheap luxury here)

transport.note: €90–€160 (rental car 5 days, or trains and regional buses)

hook: Slovakia keeps five UNESCO towns and villages within a comfortable day's drive of each other and almost nobody visits them in sequence. This is a week of three beds and long afternoons: a silver town inside a collapsed volcano, the tallest Gothic altar on earth, a burgher square with its medieval plot lines intact, and a log village where the smoke still smells of spruce. Deliberately unhurried, unfashionable, and very cheap.

snapshot.Getting there: Fly Bratislava (BTS) or Vienna (VIE, 70 km); return from Košice (KSC). Rail alternative: Bratislava–Hronská Dúbrava–Banská Štiavnica, then IC to Poprad and Spišská Nová Ves.

itinerary.title: Into the caldera
itinerary.morning: Collect the car in Bratislava and take the R1 east to Žiar nad Hronom, then the switchbacks up to Banská Štiavnica — about two and a half hours. The town sits inside a collapsed volcanic caldera, which is why the streets run at impossible angles.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk Trojičné námestie, the plague column and the **Old Castle** — a 13th-century church fortified against the Ottomans. Then up to the **New Castle**, a white watchtower with the best single view of the roofs.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at a guesthouse table. Order *kapustnica*, the sauerkraut and sausage soup, and ask about the *tajchy* — your hosts will each name a different favourite.

itinerary.title: Adits and reservoirs (Banská Štiavnica)
itinerary.morning: The **Slovak Mining Museum's Bartolomej adit** (Štôlňa Bartolomej) at the open-air museum: helmet, lamp, boots and an underground hour in a real 18th-century working [VERIFY: current adit tour times and price]. Book the first slot; groups fill the later ones.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the **Calvary** — 23 stations climbing a volcanic cone to a twin-towered upper church, restored from near-ruin over twenty years. It takes an hour up and is the single best thing in the town.
itinerary.evening: Swim in a *tajch*. **Klinger** is nearest, **Počúvadlo** the biggest and warmest. These are 18th-century mining water reservoirs built by Hell and Mikovíny to power pumps — engineering, not leisure, and now the town's swimming lakes.

itinerary.title: Across to Spiš
itinerary.morning: Drive east via Zvolen and Banská Bystrica, then the R2/D1 to Poprad — around three hours. Break at **Vlkolínec** above Ružomberok, a UNESCO log-house village of 45 dwellings, still inhabited, still without a souvenir strip [VERIFY: current Vlkolínec entry fee].
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive in Levoča and simply walk the square before the light goes. The town walls are largely complete and you can circle most of them.
itinerary.evening: Eat *pirohy* and *halušky* in a cellar restaurant off Námestie Majstra Pavla, then look at the Cage of Shame, a 16th-century iron cage on the square where scolds and drunks were displayed.

itinerary.title: The tallest altar in the world (Levoča)
itinerary.morning: The **Basilica of St James**. **Master Pavol of Levoča** carved its high altar between 1507 and 1517 — **18.6 m of limewood**, the tallest Gothic altarpiece anywhere, with the Last Supper predella and life-size apostles. Entry is by timed guided visit from the ticket office opposite; go at opening [VERIFY: current basilica ticket price and tour times].
itinerary.afternoon: The Renaissance **town hall** and the Master Pavol House museum. Then climb to the Mariánska hora pilgrimage basilica above the town for the Spiš basin panorama.
itinerary.evening: Guesthouse dinner. Ask for *bryndzové halušky* made with real sheep bryndza rather than cow-curd substitute — say *"z ovčej bryndze, prosím"*.

itinerary.title: Castle and chapter
itinerary.morning: Drive fifteen minutes to **Spišské Podhradie** and up to **Spiš Castle (Spišský hrad)**, one of the largest castle complexes in central Europe, spread over a travertine hill. Wear real shoes; the upper ward is exposed and there is no shade [VERIFY: current Spišský hrad entry fee and season].
itinerary.afternoon: Cross the valley to **Spišská Kapitula**, the walled ecclesiastical town — one street, two gates, the Romanesque St Martin's Cathedral and the canons' houses. It is silent, and takes an hour.
itinerary.evening: Back in Levoča for a wine on the square. The Spiš towns were German-settled from the 13th century, and the burgher plot widths on the square still show it.

itinerary.title: North to Šariš
itinerary.morning: Detour to **Kežmarok** for the **wooden articular church** — built 1717 without a single nail, of yew and red spruce, seating 1,500, put up under Habsburg rules that forbade stone, towers and a town-centre site for Protestants. UNESCO-listed [VERIFY: current articular church opening hours].
itinerary.afternoon: Drive to **Bardejov** via Prešov, about two hours. Walk **Radničné námestie**, ringed by gabled burgher houses, with the 1509 town hall standing free in the middle.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in a house on the square. Bardejov closes early; eat at 18:00 like the locals.

itinerary.title: Wafers and the suburbium (Bardejov)
itinerary.morning: **St Egidius (Bazilika sv. Egídia)**, an 11-altar Gothic church whose winged altarpieces survive largely in place. Climb the tower if it is open [VERIFY: current tower access].
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the **Jewish suburbium** north-west of the walls — the 1836 Old Synagogue, the ritual bath and the assembly house, one of the most complete surviving Jewish town quarters in Slovakia. Then take the bus or drive 5 km to **Bardejovské Kúpele** for the spa colonnade and a bag of *oplátky* eaten warm.
itinerary.evening: Drive or take the train to Košice, 75 km, for the flight out — or stay a last night and eat *šúľance s makom* somewhere with a tiled stove.

accommodationStrategy.name: Penzión Cosmopolitan II
accommodationStrategy.description: on the historic core within three minutes of Trojičné námestie, so you can park once and not touch the car for two days — which matters in a town where every street is a gradient. Breakfast, and staff who will tell you which tajch is warm this week.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct or Booking.com, 4–6 weeks ahead; longer for the September weekends [VERIFY: current nightly rate].

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel U Leva
accommodationStrategy.style: historic house on the main square
accommodationStrategy.description: directly on Námestie Majstra Pavla, so the basilica is a 90-second walk and you can be first through the door at opening, before the coaches from Poprad. Restaurant on site for the nights you cannot face going out.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct, 3–4 weeks ahead; it fills for the July Marian pilgrimage weekend.

accommodationStrategy.name: Penzión Semafor
accommodationStrategy.description: a short walk below the square with parking, a family kitchen doing genuine Šariš cooking, and hosts who will book you into the synagogue visit — which is not a walk-in.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct by phone or email, 2–3 weeks ahead.

logistics.connectivity: 4G/5G is good in all four towns; Vlkolínec and the upper Calvary are patchier. Free Wi-Fi in most guesthouses and on Levoča's square.
logistics.emergency: 112 nationwide. Hospitals in Banská Štiavnica (small), Poprad and Bardejov. Nothing here is remote enough to need mountain rescue, but if you walk the Štiavnické vrchy ridges, HZS is **18 300** and Slovak mountain rescue is chargeable without insurance.
logistics.weather: Continental. Spring and autumn swing 15 °C in a day; the caldera holds fog until mid-morning in September. Pack a warm layer even in June — Levoča sits at 570 m and Bardejov at 277 m, and the evenings feel it.
logistics.bookingWindows: Guesthouses 3–6 weeks. The exceptions are the first weekend of September in Banská Štiavnica (**Salamander** mining festival, when the whole town is booked out months ahead) and the Levoča pilgrimage weekend in early July [VERIFY: 2027 Salamander dates].
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are accepted in towns; carry €60–€80 cash for adit tours, church entries, village entry fees and market stalls. ATMs on every main square.
logistics.transportRules: A car makes this week; without one, use IC trains to Poprad and Prešov plus regional buses (cp.sk for timetables). If driving motorways, buy the **e-vignette** at eznamka.sk — it is plate-registered and there is no windscreen sticker. Blood-alcohol limit is **0.0‰**, absolutely.
logistics.permits: No permits. Almost every museum in Slovakia closes **Monday**; plan Monday as a driving or walking day. Vlkolínec charges a small village entry fee and is a living settlement — do not photograph through windows.

proTips: Do the Levoča basilica at opening, not after lunch. The Master Pavol altar is visited in timed groups and the mid-morning slots go to school and coach parties; the first tour of the day is often six people.

Swim at **Počúvadlo** rather than Klinger in high summer, and at Klinger in September when Počúvadlo has cooled. Locals treat the tajchy as a temperature ladder and will tell you which one is currently right.
Buy bryndza and *žinčica* at a roadside *salaš* on the Ružomberok–Poprad stretch, not in a shop. The whey is only good the day it is made, and it will not exist by afternoon.
Ask your guesthouse at breakfast whether they will cook dinner. Most will, for €10–€14 a head, and it is invariably better than the restaurant on the square.
Skip the Spiš Castle car park queue by arriving before 09:30 or after 15:30; the site is huge and thins out fast in the last two hours.
Learn *"Prosím si účet"* (the bill, please) and *"Máte domácu polievku?"* (do you have homemade soup?). Soup is the point of a Slovak lunch and is usually not on the printed menu.
If Monday falls mid-trip, use it for Vlkolínec and the Calvary — both outdoor, both open, both better empty.

raw.Village and town squares by name: **Trojičné námestie** in Banská Štiavnica — a sloping triangle of merchant houses around the 1759 plague column, with the Old Castle above and the New Castle on its own knoll. **Námestie Majstra Pavla** in Levoča, a vast rectangle holding the Basilica of St James, the Renaissance town hall with its arcades, the Evangelical church and the **Cage of Shame**. **Radničné námestie** in Bardejov, the most intact Gothic-burgher square in Slovakia, closed at the top by St Egidius. **Vlkolínec** has no square at all — it has one lane, 45 log houses, a wooden belfry and a two-storey log bell tower.
raw.Market days and where to buy: Levoča's produce market runs on the lower square most mornings, busiest Friday and Saturday [VERIFY: current Levoča market days]. Banská Štiavnica has a Saturday farmers' market on Trojičné námestie in season [VERIFY: current market schedule]. Bardejov's market sits below the square by the bus station. Buy *bryndza* — the salted sheep's cheese with PGI protection — direct from a *salaš* rather than a supermarket, and drink the *žinčica* whey alongside it while it is fresh.
raw.Named crafts: **Modra majolica** (blue-and-white tin-glazed earthenware, still hand-painted at the Modra workshop). **Čičmany patterning** — the white lime geometry painted onto dark log walls in the Žilina region, now Slovakia's most-reproduced folk motif. **Bardejov's oplátky**, the wafer-thin spa wafers sold at Bardejovské Kúpele. Woodcarving and gilding around Levoča, a direct inheritance of Master Pavol's workshop.
raw.Boutique and small stays: Everything here is a *penzión* or a converted burgher house; there is no international chain outside Košice. Expect €35–€60 a night for a double with breakfast, and dinner cooked to order if you ask in the morning.
raw.Pacing rule: Three bases in seven nights: Banská Štiavnica (nights 1–2), Levoča (nights 3–5), Bardejov (nights 6–7). Never more than one relocation every two days, and two of the three relocations are under two hours.
